anti_patterns: Treating an unsigned single-server inference endpoint as an oracle, so one compromised API key or model host can move money on-chain
Passing raw model text into state-changing logic without a schema, confidence threshold, or staleness bound, so a hedged or outdated answer executes irreversibly
Binding the request to neither model version nor input hash, so the attested output cannot be tied to what the agent actually asked and outputs are replayable across tasks
Blocking the agent loop synchronously on fulfillment instead of modeling pending/expired/fulfilled states, so a slow DON round-trip stalls the whole plan
Skipping fee, callback-gas, and timeout budgeting, so requests fail silently when the subscription runs dry or fulfillment exceeds the gas limit
Accepting fulfillment in a callback that does not check request ID, caller (router/coordinator), and freshness, leaving the contract open to spoofed or stale callbacks
avoid_when: The decision must settle within one block or a tight latency budget, since inference plus oracle aggregation spans multiple blocks
The inference result is advisory only and a human reviews every output before any on-chain effect, in which case the attestation machinery is pure overhead
The action is fully reversible off-chain and needs no settlement guarantee, so a direct API call from the agent suffices
No oracle network supports the required model or input size within the fee budget, and a custom attester set cannot be recruited
benefits: Gives a deterministic VM access to nondeterministic AI compute without breaking consensus, since inference runs off-chain and only the attested receipt settles on-chain
DON-level execution plus OCR aggregation means a minority of faulty or malicious nodes cannot dictate the response the contract acts on
Binding each request to model identity and input hash makes outputs auditable and replay-resistant: the contract can prove which model answered which question
Threshold decryption and subscription billing keep API keys and fees off the consumer contract, so secrets stay sealed and contracts hold no LINK
Pending/expired/fulfilled request states let the agent plan around latency instead of blocking, with timeouts and refunds as first-class branches
Verification policy (quorum, accepted attesters, proof-verifier address) lives on-chain as config, so trust assumptions are explicit and upgradable
best_practices: Bind every request to model digest plus input hash and verify the binding in the fulfillment callback before any state change
Gate execution on a verification policy checked on-chain: attester threshold, freshness window, and request-ID/caller match against the router or coordinator
Model the full request lifecycle in the agent plan (pending, fulfilled, expired, disputed) with timeout, retry-with-backoff, and refund branches
Budget fees and callback gas up front via the subscription account and cost simulation, and fail closed when the budget is exhausted
Keep raw tensors and prose off-chain; settle only hashes, labels, scores, and metadata plus an event pointing at the full artifact
Log request ID, model version, input hash, attester set, and freshness at fulfillment so any executed action is reconstructable
Prefer replicated inference consensus or TEE/zk attestation over single-node feeds for any action that moves funds or changes protocol parameters
component_types: inference request builder with model, input-hash, and budget binding
consumer contract with request lifecycle state machine
oracle coordinator and router contracts with fulfillment callback
decentralized oracle network executor with threshold decryption
aggregation and attestation relay (OCR median plus signatures)
gated action executor and timeout or refund handler
context: An autonomous agent must turn an AI inference result into an on-chain effect — a payout, a parameter update, a gated tool action — but the EVM is a closed deterministic VM: it cannot call HTTP APIs, cannot run a model, and meters every byte of storage and every signature check in gas. The agent therefore needs a bridge that runs heavy nondeterministic inference off-chain and settles only a verified receipt on-chain. This pattern is that bridge: the agent builds an inference request bound to a model identity and an input hash with a fee and staleness budget; the consumer contract emits the request and escrows the fee via a subscription account; a decentralized oracle network (for example Chainlink Functions DONs, Ritual Infernet nodes, or Oraichain validators) executes the inference off-chain, aggregates independent node results with OCR-style consensus, and relays one attested response back through a coordinator/router fulfillment callback; the contract verifies attester threshold, request-ID match, and freshness, then executes the gated action — otherwise it times out, refunds, or disputes. It differs from a plain price-feed oracle in what is attested: not an observable datum but an unobservable computation, which forces the extra binding of model version plus input and an execution-verification dimension (replicated consensus, TEE attestation, or zk proof checked as policy). Scope boundary: this pattern owns the request-attest-deliver-gate loop; proof construction and fraud-proof arbitration over inference execution belong to the sibling onchain-ai-inference concern and appear here only as a verification-policy option.
design_principles: Never execute on an unattested output: verification of the receipt precedes any state-changing effect
Bind the output to the exact question asked — model digest plus input hash — or the attestation proves nothing
Treat the oracle set as an explicit trust assumption encoded on-chain, not as ambient infrastructure
Design for asynchrony: inference finality lags chain finality, so pending and expired are normal states, not errors
Settle minimal commitments on-chain and keep bulk artifacts off-chain behind content addresses
Fail closed on ambiguity: stale, under-quorum, or mismatched receipts must block the action, never degrade into trust
name: ai-oracle
references: Chainlink Labs, Chainlink Functions Architecture, n.d. -- https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-functions/resources/architecture
technology_stack: Ritual Infernet SDK and infernet-ml workflows
Oraichain oracle scripts and validator test-case verification
EVM subscription billing and threshold-decryption secrets management
tradeoffs: Every inference round-trip spans blocks and bills a LINK subscription plus callback gas, so high-frequency decisions become slow and expensive
The oracle set is a residual trust point: quorum thresholds and attester reputation bound but do not eliminate collusion or model-host manipulation
Request/response schemas, model versioning, and input-hash discipline are mandatory coupling between agent, contract, and oracle operators — drift breaks fulfillment
Staleness is structural: a model answer verified three blocks late can be correct yet wrong to act on, forcing explicit freshness windows and reject paths
Secrets and inputs that pass through DON execution need threshold encryption and careful redaction, since replicated execution widens exposure
Debugging crosses three failure domains (agent plan, oracle network, contract callback), so a failed action needs request-ID tracing across all of them
use_cases: A DeFi risk agent that requests an off-chain credit-risk inference and only rebalances collateral when a quorum-attested score arrives within its freshness window
A parametric-insurance agent that feeds sensor plus model-derived event classification through a DON and pays out on the attested label
An on-chain governance agent that summarizes proposal text off-chain and casts a vote only after the summary receipt verifies against the bound input hash
A dynamic-NFT agent that generates attribute updates via model inference and mints the change when the fulfillment callback authenticates
